youtube.title: What If GTA Physics Worked in Real Life? #Shorts
youtube.description:
What if GTA physics worked in real life? Jump off a skyscraper, roll, and walk away. Remy runs three tests.

Test 1, the fall: a skydiver reaches top speed after about 12 seconds of falling, around 200 km/h. That's terminal velocity, when air resistance pushes back as hard as gravity pulls. Parachutes exist for a reason. Remy takes the stairs.
Test 2, the car: a crash at just 50 km/h hits your body like falling from the third floor of a building. Double the speed and the crash energy becomes four times bigger (kinetic energy grows with speed squared). Seat belts spread the stop across your hips and chest.
Test 3, walking: more than 95% of pedestrians hit by a car at 30 km/h survive; at 50 km/h, about 85%. That's why many towns put 30 zones near schools.

In the game, you respawn. Out here, you get one save file. Which GTA move would hurt the most in real life?

Sources:
- Terminal velocity of a skydiver (~53-56 m/s, about 190-200 km/h): The Physics Factbook: https://hypertextbook.com/facts/1998/JianHuang.shtml
- Mathematics of skydiving (terminal velocity after roughly 12 s of free fall): EBSCO Research Starters: https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/sports-and-leisure/mathematics-skydiving
- A 50 km/h crash compared with falling from the third floor: Road to Zero (Victoria, Australia), Crash forces: https://www.roadtozero.vic.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0005/392477/Background-Crash-Forces-Elevator_v06.pdf
- Pedestrian survival by impact speed (>95% at 30 km/h, ~85% at 50 km/h): SWOV: https://www.swov.nl/en/node/16371 and European Commission road safety: https://road-safety.transport.ec.europa.eu/statistics-and-analysis/statistics-and-analysis-archive/pedestrians/no-speed-no-mass-and-no-protection_en
- Crash energy grows with the square of speed: kinetic energy = 1/2 m v^2 (basic physics).

Don't try any of this. Always wear your seat belt and slow down near schools.
Remy is fictional. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two. No game footage, art or logos are used.
